Body Composition
Height and weight, though crucial components of nutrition as-
sessment, are only gross measurements and cannot distinguish 
among body compartments. It is not unusual, then, for very 
muscular individuals to fall into an overweight or obese catego-
rization when only height and weight are used in the nutrition 
assessment. Measurements of skinfolds, waist circumference, 
and other body composition techniques allow the clinician to 
make a more thorough and complete nutrition assessment. 
However, these are not routinely done in most clinical settings
where acute care is the primary goal. In settings where clients
are followed for a length of time, these assessments are clini-
cally useful.
